findings.defect: The new per-request read-stop guards do not cover repository-authority or authorization requests. RepositoryAccess captures a connection via CurrentAsync and then sends /repos and installation/repository-page requests without checking that the session record, connection reference, and generation are still current before each request. CurrentAsync likewise can send its refresh exchange or /user verification request after disconnect/replacement races; its post-response checks only prevent retaining the result. Issue context invokes this authority path before its issue reads, and IssueEvidence invokes it again before evidence reads. The four RED/GREEN cases cover report, inventory, ZIP, and related-PR/check interruptions, but not a disconnect during these authority/authorization requests.
findings.consequence: After a disconnect or account replacement, the prior connected-user token can still be used for additional GitHub requests during the permission-check phase. This is the same read-stop/account-isolation violation the checkpoint intends to close, occurring before the individually guarded issue/evidence requests.
findings.fix: Capture connection and generation for authority checks and verify live session, connection, and generation immediately before every outbound authority request, including each pagination request. Ensure CurrentAsync does not initiate refresh or /user requests for a stale connection, and abort the authority operation on mismatch. Add deterministic disconnect/replacement tests at each authority request boundary and during due authorization verification.

findings.defect: Every successful page read calls readEvidence, whose handler calls GetIssueContextHandler again for the same page. That refetches both the issue and the conversation page (including the comments endpoint) after the browser has already fetched that page. Across the documented 10-page view this performs up to 20 conversation-page requests, not the proposal's hard maximum of 10; it also doubles the associated issue reads.
findings.consequence: The implementation exceeds the accepted per-view source-request and downloaded-data bounds and repeats source reads unnecessarily, weakening the explicit pagination stop and increasing provider load. The browser's retained-comment cap does not limit these duplicate server-side reads.
findings.fix: Avoid having evidence projection refetch the issue/conversation page already read for the view. Reuse a validated page/reference set for evidence, or separate evidence discovery from conversation loading while retaining fresh permission checks and the existing snapshot/account binding. Add a test asserting at most one conversation API request per displayed page, including evidence loading.
